Join the team as Twilio’s next New Business Account Executive 4 on our High Tech team!

About the job

This position is needed to lead prospecting, solution selling and closing new business opportunities across our Messaging, Voice and Email products. In this role, you will be directly responsible for expanding our messaging business with some of the largest and fastest growing mid-market and enterprise companies in the High Tech vertical. New Business Account Executives are experts in the CPaaS ecosystem and Twilio’s product offerings. This role is highly cross functional, with deep integration with product management, carrier relations, finance, and solutions engineering teams.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

Drive new customer acquisition, while being assigned a quota for iACV (incremental Account Contract Value)

Own highly analytical and consultative sales cycles to win business in competitive vendor sourcing cycles with Twilio’s messaging (e.g. SMS, MMS, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Google Business Messages, Account Security, etc.), voice and email solutions.

Work with customers across assigned verticals (Financial Services) to understand their business and technical requirements, and match them to the capabilities of Twilio’s communications API platform, designing a solution for their specific use cases.

Work with teams in Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Operations to design mutually beneficial contracts to address customer requirements, while balancing the needs of our business.

Be passionate about what you do, think outside the box, and use world-class interpersonal and communication skills to present complex contractual, technical, and financial details to prospects in a way that builds confidence and comfort in the proposed solution.

Balance competing priorities and manage multiple projects and deals at the same time.

Partner cross functionally with sales, services, product, and finance to develop long range territory strategies and sales plans.

Act as the voice of the customer to Twilio’s product and carrier relations teams.

Demonstrate a strong understanding of the CPaaS industry - staying up to date on key industry initiatives and new capabilities - on behalf of your customers and the wider Twilio go-to-market organization.

Generate and maintain an accurate pipeline and forecast utilizing our CRM, Salesforce.

Stay current with industry changes and collaborate with your team and peers to learn and share best practices

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:

Possess a total of 8 years of tech sales experience, with a minimum of 6 years in a closing role

Directly selling technical SaaS or CPaaS and experience solution selling and multi-threading

Experience outbound prospecting into new accounts and a strong “hunter” mentality for bringing in Mid-Market and Enterprise sized accounts

Technical solutions selling experience working with real customers and prospects, listening to them, and solving problems

Comfortable working with business and highly technical leaders, while influencing their understanding and building supportive partnerships

Analytical account development strategy based on using data to find opportunities and prove value

Demonstrated track record of managing business forecasts and financial models

Entrepreneurial mindset with appetite to define process and build programs

Record of delivering market driven results, especially to scale and enterprise customers

Excellent verbal and written communication skills (English)

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent years of experience

Desired:

Deep experience working with telecom companies, including CPAAS, SMS aggregators, carriers, or global communications platforms.

Domain expertise from a highly quantitative industry such as DevOps, Fintech, advertising optimization, investment banking, security or commodity trading especially in non-standard segments.

Software, SaaS, CPaas or PaaS selling experienc

Location

This role will be remote and located in the United States.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 20% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Minnesota or Vermont : $110,160 - $137,700.

Based in Washington D.C., Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay Area): $116,280- $145,350.

Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or the San Francisco Bay area, California: $122,400 - $153,300. This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

This role is eligible to earn commissions.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until November 20th, 2026, but may change based on business needs.

Join the team as Twilio’s next Architect on our Data Substrate team

About the job

Twilio runs on data, and the platform underneath it is entering a major shift. Open table formats, the convergence of lakes and warehouses, tightening privacy regulation, and AI workloads are all changing what a data platform has to do. We’re hiring an Architect to set our direction through that shift and to make sure the systems we build over the next 3-5 years are the right ones.

You’ll own the technical strategy for our data platform, spanning storage, lake and lakehouse architecture, catalog and governance, and privacy-by-design. You’ll work across org boundaries, setting standards that dozens of teams build on and raising the technical bar for the engineers around you.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

Own the architecture and multi-year technical strategy for the data platform, including the lake/lakehouse, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and governance, and keep them coherent as one platform rather than separate systems. Define where each engine fits (for example, ClickHouse versus open table formats on object storage) and the migration path between them.

Make and document the major design decisions (ADRs, RFCs) on storage and open table formats, catalog strategy, compute engines, tenancy, data placement, and build-versus-adopt tradeoffs, with cost and performance at petabyte scale as explicit design constraints.

Set the reference architectures for how our core storage and query engines (ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and lake engines) are deployed, tuned, scaled and operated as shared platforms, including capacity, cost, tenant isolation, and upgrade strategy.

Define the reliability model for the platform: availability targets, failure domains, disaster recovery, observability, and incident response patterns that teams can adopt.

Build privacy and compliance into the architecture, not onto it. Design deletion and right-to-erasure, retention, data residency, and PII classification so they work across the platform’s storage layers, backups, and derived datasets, including data that arrives from upstream streaming systems.

Drive data governance: classification, catalog and metadata, lineage, access control integrated with our authentication and authorization systems, data contracts, quality and integrity standards, and a catalog teams actually use.

Review designs and technical direction across the org, and act as the escalation point on hard distributed-systems and performance problems.

Mentor principal and senior engineers, and grow architectural judgment across the org, not only within one squad.

Partner with product, security, infrastructure and consuming teams to turn business needs into platform roadmaps, and say no or re-sequence when the tradeoffs require it.

Track emerging data technologies (such as streaming-first architectures, federated query, and AI-ready data layers) and bring forward the ones worth adopting, with evidence from prototypes or benchmarks.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

15+ years of experience in software development or a related field, with at least 8 years in an architecture or senior technical leadership role.

Proven track record of architecting and delivering large-scale data platforms and setting their technical strategy, on cloud infrastructure such as AWS, deployed with Kubernetes, Terraform and Helm.

Deep expertise in storage and compute for analytical data: columnar and open table formats, lake and lakehouse architecture, partitioning, indexing, query planning, and how the choices affect cost and performance at petabyte scale.

Breadth across data storage and retrieval technologies, with hands-on depth in at least two of: analytical/OLAP engines (e.g., ClickHouse), search engines (e.g., ElasticSearch/OpenSearch), and lake or distributed processing engines (e.g., Spark, Trino, Flink). You can reason about when to use each, how they interoperate, and how to migrate between them.

Working knowledge of streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) and how they interact with downstream storage.

Practical experience designing data governance at scale: data classification, catalog and metadata management, lineage, and access control integrated with authentication and authorization systems.

Practical experience implementing privacy and compliance requirements (deletion, retention, residency) across a large, heterogeneous data estate.

Proficiency in one or more of Python, Java, and Go.

Track record of writing and driving architecture decisions across multiple teams, and of changing the direction of an organization’s technical roadmap through influence rather than authority.

Experience elevating engineering standards and mentoring senior engineers across teams.

Demonstrated commitment to operational excellence: architecting for high availability, observability and incident response in distributed systems, and being credible when a platform is failing in production.

Strong written and verbal communication, including making a complex tradeoff clear to engineers and to senior leadership.

Desired:

Experience operating one of these engines (e.g., ClickHouse, ElasticSearch) at scale, including replication, sharding, ingestion behavior, and multi-tenant isolation.

Experience with catalog and metadata systems (e.g., Unity Catalog, Glue, Polaris, DataHub) and open table format catalog strategy.

Experience with a platform migration across domains or ownership models, such as moving from central to domain-owned data.

A track record of measurable cost optimization on large data platforms.

Networking and network security knowledge.

Location

This role will be remote, and based in the United States.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

About the job

We are actively recruiting for this role to fill an existing vacancy. This position will be responsible for working constructively with our customers and partners to resolve billing issues and fraudulent misuse of services.

We are seeking a sharp, highly data-oriented, and tenacious Fraud Specialist to join our team. Unlike a traditional billing or collections role focused on routine outreach or simple invoice review, this position is a hybrid of financial investigation, root cause analysis, and strategic dispute negotiation. In this role, you will look for billing discrepancies, investigate Artificially Inflated Traffic (AIT) or IRSF (International Revenue Share Fraud), dig deep into messaging and call data, project manage high-value customer and vendor disputes, and build data-backed cases to resolve discrepancies. You will build dashboards to communicate key metrics and drive action. If you love solving complex data puzzles, negotiating with external parties, and finding win-win outcomes, this is the role for you.

You will be part of a company that is the category leader in Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS), an organization working with the largest customers and partners, and a team of operators and former consultants that have delivered exceptional impact. If you have an extreme owner / founder mindset and a desire to solve big challenges, you’ll find yourself at home.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

Advise account managers, accounting, and management on best practices to handle billing disputes

Negotiate with customers and carriers with an understanding of resolution levers available as per contractual terms and industry norms

Identify, analyze, and handle fraudulent misuse (such as Artificially Inflated Traffic) and billing errors (such as rate differences) with both vendors and customers

Own the end-to-end lifecycle of customer and vendor disputes from intake of disputes to initiating disputes, tracking progress, and ensuring timely, documented resolution

Uncover and resolve discrepancies, overcharges, and unpaid balances with carriers and customers due to quantities, rates, currency, and other root causes

Dig into call and messaging data to identify why bills don’t match or find evidence of fraud

Build dashboards that communicate key metrics related to the lifecycle of disputes

Read contracts and interpret what should be the invoice versus what it is

Act as the primary point of contact to negotiate dispute resolutions, settlements, and payment terms in accordance with company practices

Partner closely with data analytics, engineering, and accounting to reconcile accounts

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. 8+ years of professional experience in telecom operations, fraud operations, customer success, vendor management, procurement, collections, or consulting.

Sharp written and verbal communication skills.

Experience negotiating disputes constructively with customers or vendors.

Experience in collections, dispute resolution, or billing analysis.

Experience in project management.

Experience wrangling data with Excel / Google Sheets, Looker or SQL.

Understanding of the A2P SMS ecosystem, international traffic routing, international revenue share fraud (IRSF), artificially inflated traffic (AIT) and the ecosystem profit chains.

Understanding of Call Detail Records (CDRs) and ability to build strong dispute case files.

Experience working with workflow platforms like Airtable or building dashboards.

Experience in telecom, technology, or consulting industries.

Experience with advanced data analysis like Python or scripting

This position is needed to build and scale the pipelines that turn raw conversation data into structured, searchable customer memory, and the evaluation systems that keep that memory accurate as the product evolves.

You'll join the Conversation Memory team, which builds the memory layer behind Twilio's Conversational AI platform: the systems that extract what matters from millions of conversations, resolve it to the right customer, and retrieve it in milliseconds when an agent needs it. Memory that is wrong, stale, or crossed between customers is worse than no memory at all, so quality measurement is a first-class part of the work.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

Build the extraction pipeline that turns raw data into structured memory, tuning the LLM prompts and schemas that decide what an AI agent remembers about a customer and what it forgets.

Own the retrieval path that answers "what do we know about this person?" in milliseconds, working with embeddings, vector search, and ranking

Contribute to the eval systems that tell us whether memory is actually getting better, turning a fuzzy question of quality into benchmarks and regression gates that run before every change ships.

Diagnose production issues across the ingestion, extraction, and indexing path using logs, metrics, and traces.

Partner with Product and ML teams to translate customer problems into system changes and evaluation criteria.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Payroll Tax and Compliance Analyst (based remotely in Ireland) to support payroll employment taxes, regulatory adherence, and mobility compliance across our APJ and EMEA regions. As a fast-growing tech company, our workforce is highly mobile. Working closely with internal stakeholders and external tax/payroll advisors, you will help ensure accurate tax withholding, social security application, and statutory compliance across multiple jurisdictions. Reporting to the Director, Global Payroll, you will execute compliance workflows, flag potential risks, and support seamless payroll operations for a dynamic, global team.

Tax Oversight: Coordinate recurring payroll tax compliance, statutory filings, and general ledger reconciliations across APJ and EMEA (covering Ireland, UK, Sweden, Spain, France, Poland, Germany, Estonia, Belgium, Australia, India, Singapore, Japan, and Hong Kong) in partnership with local payroll vendors.

Mobility Tracking: Monitor employee movement, international business travel, and cross-border transfers to ensure timely and accurate payroll tax withholding and shadow payroll reporting.

Nexus Assessment: Track remote worker locations and cross-border travel data, flagging potential corporate tax footprint or Permanent Establishment (PE) triggers to Corporate Tax and Legal teams for review.

Social Security: Administer local social security contributions and coordinate Certificates of Coverage (A1 forms and bilateral totalisation agreements) for internationally mobile employees.

Regulatory Research: Monitor upcoming tax law changes, statutory rate updates, and local filing requirements across active jurisdictions, updating internal compliance calendars and SOPs accordingly.

Agency Management: Serve as a day-to-day operational contact for local payroll partners, external tax advisors, and auditors, preparing supporting schedules and resolving routine tax authority queries.

Year-End Reporting: Execute and track country-specific year-end tax reporting processes across APJ and EMEA, ensuring timely statutory submissions and employee tax certificate distribution.

Process Optimization: Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and improve data accuracy for mobile employee tax adjustments and compliance tracking.

Geographic Scope: Working knowledge of EMEA and/or APJ statutory payroll taxes, filings, and social security frameworks.

Mobility Expertise: Solid understanding of cross-border employee taxation, shadow payroll concepts, trailing liabilities, and remote work compliance considerations.

Technical Skills: Proficiency with global payroll and HRIS platforms (e.g., Workday, Deel) and strong spreadsheet/data reconciliation skills.

We’re looking for a Staff Product Designer (L4) to define the user experience for Twilio Identity: customer identity (authentication, Hosted Login, and user management) and Agent Identity, which lets developers open their apps and APIs, including remote MCP servers, to AI agents with user consent, scoped access, and human approval for sensitive actions over Twilio channels like SMS and RCS.

You’ll be the lead designer on a small, senior team, working with product and engineering from the first sketch. Own Identity UX End to End: Lead the experience for developer onboarding and configuration in One Console, Hosted Login, and end-user authentication flows.

Make Self-Serve Fast: Shorten the path from sign-up to a working integration, so developers can evaluate and adopt Twilio Identity without talking to sales.

Translate Protocol Complexity: Turn OAuth, tokens, scopes, and approval flows into clear mental models for developers and plain-language choices for end users.

Partner Before the PRD: Work with PM and engineering from problem framing through launch, co-owning scope and tradeoffs while holding a high bar for craft.

Twilio is looking for a Staff Site Reliability Engineer to join our Platform Engineering organization. SRE owns production health and resiliency at Twilio — we are accountable for whether our services stay available, performant, and recoverable for the customers who build their businesses on us. SREs here are software engineers who focus on reliability: you will architect systems with reliability designed in from the outset, define the SLIs and SLOs that determine whether we are meeting customer expectations, and build the automation that keeps our infrastructure efficiently ahead of capacity and performance demand.

At the Staff SRE you work without day-to-day guidance, applying deep subject-matter knowledge and industry-leading practice to improve the products, processes, and services that Twilio runs on. You will own the reliability posture of significant parts of our production estate. Your impact will be felt across multiple teams rather than within one.

Own the reliability posture of production services in your area — availability, latency, capacity, efficiency, performance, and the monitoring and alerting that makes them visible

Define, instrument, and operate against SLIs and SLOs, and use error budgets to drive engineering priorities

Identify trends and problem areas that threaten stability, and provide a path forward to mitigate risk before it reaches customers

Drive down repair items and prevent classes of incidents rather than resolving them one at a time

Improve detection, response, and recovery — reducing time to acknowledge, engage, mitigate, and restore, with fewer people pulled in

Design for failure: strengthen failure domains, validate recovery paths, and make production changes safer to ship and safer to roll back

Write post-mortems that identify true root causes, and drive the follow-up work to completion

Oversee efforts to identify, diagnose, report, and document production problems across all reliability dimensions

Write, configure, and deploy code that measurably improves service reliability — maintainable, reviewed, documented, and well tested

Orchestrate complex changes across systems and services, documenting design changes, technical decisions, migration plans, and upgrades
